summary: The stage-2 design (S = 1024 // B oversubscription plus a one-tile-ahead register prefetch of K/V, num_stages=1) is sound and within the rules. It is a reasonable next step for the rewrite, but porting fa3-hdim128-head-pairing to decode_layer is the better use of a check: it is measured, it also covers full verify_16/32, and its estimated headline gain (~2.0%) beats this stage's best case (~1.5%). With 4 decode checks left, dispatch the head-pairing port first and re-base this rewrite's milestone 2 on paired-FA3 time.
justification: Mechanism: stage 1's profile (e82b11f9d9f64b23) puts _full_decode_split_kernel at 200.8 us (decode_16 full) and 394.8 us (decode_32 full), about 1.63-1.66 TB/s over ~328/655 MB. Unpaired FA3 is 188.8/374.4 us, and the floors are 137.5/208.1 us for the whole layer, so attention alone is far above its own floor. The grid diagnosis holds: 272/288 CTAs is ~2 per SM, 288 > 264 leaves a tail, and under spread=agentic split_len comes from page_table.shape[1], so the splits of short requests empty out early. S = 1024 // B (64 at B=16, 32 at B=32, still 128 at B=1) lets the empty splits drain and refill the SM slots. That is plausible. Register prefetch costs ~32 extra regs/thread (2 x uint8 [64,128] over 128 threads). Smem is ~32 KB/CTA for the bf16 K/V dot operands. Both fit 4 CTAs/SM on H100, so the 'about 64 KB in flight per SM' claim is credible. Expected directions agree with TASK.md: only the full decode_16/32 shapes change (weight 16 each in their loads), decode_1 stays at S=128, and sliding and verify stay on FA3, so they are controls. WEAKEST LINK: the premise that bytes in flight, not the page-size-1 128-byte row gather, is the limit. LESSONS says full decode 'reaches only 1.3-1.7 TB/s: the page-size-1 row gather is the limit'. The only paired-row reference point is FA3 with head pairing in muse_attention_decode, at 165.2/307.0 us, about 2.0-2.1 TB/s. The milestone of <= 150/<= 300 us (>= 2.2 TB/s) therefore asks this Triton kernel to beat the best paired gather measured on this hardware, from a stage that is today ~20-30% behind it. A second weak point: stage 1 already ran num_stages=3. If Triton's pipeliner already overlapped those indirect loads, dropping to num_stages=1 with a manual one-tile prefetch may not add bytes in flight. The 2x claim assumes the compiler pipelined nothing. Read kernel-1 bandwidth against stage 1's 1.63/1.66 TB/s to tell. Combine cost: 4 MB of partials written and read, BLOCK_S 64/32, ~2-3 us. That is small and correctly counted in the bar.
confounders: marlin-block-m-cap-16: no confound on the judged quantity. It changes Marlin MoE block_size_m (verify shapes only); the rewrite is judged on _full_decode_split_kernel + combine time in profile top_kernels, which shares no launches or memory traffic with Marlin. Headline-only noise.

sglang-pipeline-parity-router-hilo-m8: no confound. It sets the surrounding pipeline (FusedQKNorm, cache store, q to FP8) that produces q8/k_cache, but the FP8 q and cache layout are inputs to both stage 1 and stage 2 unchanged, so kernel-time deltas are attributable to this change.
interference: No companions. This is a rewrite stage judged on its own kernel time against stage 1's 200.8/394.8 us and FA3's 188.8/374.4 us, and the next stage is the follow-up. A control splitting oversubscription from prefetch (e.g. S=1024//B with stage 1's loop) would attribute the two sub-changes. But with 4 decode checks left it costs more than it tells, and stage 1's profile already gives the before-number for both. Neither landed hypothesis touches attention, so ab-revert or ab-tune would show nothing. If kernel-1 bandwidth comes back under ~2 TB/s, the risk section's next step (BLOCK_N=128/num_warps=8 or a two-deep ring) is the right follow-up, not a companion.
rules_flags: None blocking. Precision: FP8 q and FP8 K/V are widened exactly to bf16 for tl.dot, and P is bf16 for PV (FA3 itself rounds P lower), so this matches the stage-1 path that passed 13/13.

Every key: the loop bound and masks are unchanged, so every t < cache_seqlens[b] is visited exactly once. Past-end prefetches are fully masked (other=0) and -1 page entries are never dereferenced. The rotation must carry valid with its tile (as the hypothesis says), or a past-end tile would score as 0 instead of -inf. Required: test batch 33 ctx 20000 spread mixed (S=31, many empty splits) and batch 1 ctx 3000 (PAGE=64).

No host syncs and no input-derived caching: S comes from B (a Python int), and split_len comes from page_table.shape[1]. Scratch is allocated per call from shapes. prepare() already warms every BLOCK_S up to 128, which covers BLOCK_S 64 and 32.
open_questions: LEVER COMPARISON (answer: head-pairing is the better lever for decode_layer). In muse_attention_decode, fa3-hdim128-head-pairing took FA3 full decode_16/32 from 194.5/377.9 to 165.2/307.0 us (-15%/-19%) and full verify_16/32 from 198.3/383.1 to 173.0/309.4 us, and lost 27-35% at batch 1 (pad/unpad launches). In decode_layer, FA3 is 188.8/374.4 us on full decode_16/32 and 191.9/374.0 us on full verify_16/32. Scaling by those ratios saves ~29/~71/~25/~72 us x weight 16. That is ~2.5%/5.3%/1.3%/2.6% on the decode_16/decode_32/verify_16/verify_32 load times, about +2.0% on the 6-load geomean, if it is gated on batch > 1 so decode_1 and verify_1 keep the unpaired call. This stage, even at its milestones (150/300 us), saves ~39/~74 us on decode only, about +1.5% on the headline, with far more uncertainty. The pairing port is a ~30-line, already-correct patch (view k/v_cache as [pages, page, Hkv/2, 128], zero-padded FP8 q, slice the output, scheduler_metadata=None). Recommend minting 'fa3-hdim128-head-pairing-full-batched' for decode_layer (full layers, batch > 1, decode + verify) and spending one of the 4 checks on it before this stage.

If head pairing lands, the incumbent for this rewrite becomes paired FA3 (~160/~304 us est. on decode_16/32), not 188.8/374.4. Stage 1 already uses the same paired 128-byte gather and is ~25-30% behind that, so milestone 2 (<= 150/<= 300 us) barely clears the new incumbent. Should stage 2 still be run, or should the rewrite be parked until paired FA3's kernel bandwidth is read from the profile?

Does decode_layer's kernel_fn pass the judge's scheduler_metadata to FA3 on full layers? The attention port had to drop it for the paired geometry; check that dropping it in decode_layer does not add a metadata launch that eats the gain at batch 16.

Did stage 1's num_stages=3 actually pipeline the indirect K/V loads? If it did, switching to num_stages=1 plus manual prefetch adds little; compare kernel-1 bytes/time with stage 1's 1.63/1.66 TB/s to separate the oversubscription effect from the prefetch effect.
How long are the requests under spread=agentic at B=16/32? If most requests are near 80000 tokens, the 'short splits free their slots' argument is weak and the gain must come from residency alone.
